_comment: Physical and mathematical quantities that more than one post may state, each with its accepted value. www/scripts/claims.mjs (consistency) and claims-status.mjs collect every number a post states whose symbol or surrounding words match `match` (a case-insensitive regular expression) and whose value falls in `range`, and require it to round to `value` (known to within `ulp`, when given) at the precision the post states. A post that states the quantity with a different value, or two posts that disagree, fail claims:status. Bounds (`over 1.17`) are not statements of the value and are skipped. Add a quantity when a second post starts stating it.

quantities.name: critical temperature of the square-lattice Ising model, 2/ln(1 + sqrt 2), in J/k_B
Onsager-Yang spontaneous magnetization at T = 1.8 J/k_B
fastest cold-beam two-stream growth rate, 1/(2 sqrt 2), in units of the plasma frequency
quantities.source: cold symmetric two-beam dispersion relation (e.g. Chen, Introduction to Plasma Physics, sec. 6.6)

quantities.name: real frequency of the Landau-damped Langmuir root at k lambda_D = 0.5, in omega_p
quantities.source: mpmath root of the Maxwellian dispersion relation (posts/refs/landau_root.py); Canosa, J. Comput. Phys. 13, 158 (1973)

quantities.name: Landau damping rate at k lambda_D = 0.5, in omega_p
quantities.source: mpmath root of the Maxwellian dispersion relation (posts/refs/landau_root.py)

quantities.name: Gibbs overshoot as a fraction of the jump, Si(pi)/pi - 1/2
quantities.source: Gibbs, Nature 59, 606 (1899); Hewitt and Hewitt, Arch. Hist. Exact Sci. 21, 129 (1979)

quantities.name: peak of the square wave's partial sums, (2/pi) Si(pi)
RHF energy of water in 6-31G at the posts' geometry, hartree
years to double at 7% compounded once a year, ln 2 / ln 1.07
years to double at 7% a year compounded monthly, ln 2 / (12 ln(1 + 0.07/12))
years to double at 7% a year compounded continuously, ln 2 / 0.07
largest mass of a star of free neutrons (Oppenheimer-Volkoff), solar masses
quantities.source: Narain, Schaffner-Bielich and Mishustin, Phys. Rev. D 74, 063003 (2006)
